name: Isle of Man
summary: The Isle of Man is not in the EU and has had no EU free movement since 31 December 2020. British and Irish citizens may live here freely under the Common Travel Area (they still need a work permit to work unless exempt or an 'Isle of Man worker'). Everyone else, EU and US citizens included, needs a visa. There is no investor, retirement or digital nomad visa (Tier 1 Investor is closed). The open routes are the Start-up visa (no investment threshold, 2 years 4 months, no settlement), the Innovator visa (at least GBP 50,000 of investment funds, endorsed by the Department for Enterprise, settlement after 3 years) and the Worker Migrant visa (an Island employer, salary at least GBP 25,447.50).
naturalisation: British citizenship under the British Nationality Act 1981, applied for through the Isle of Man Nationality Service, normally after settlement (indefinite leave to remain); naturalisation fee GBP 1,858.20 (gov.im, accessed 17 October 2026). The usual UK residence period (5 years, with ILR held 12 months) was not stated on the gov.im page read. Irish citizens have a simplified route since 24 September 2025.
dual_citizenship_note: Not verified from a fetched source.

routes.fees_note: No immigration fee. Work permit application: GBP 60 paid by the employer (gov.im page last updated 31 October 2017; the June 2024 guide repeats GBP 60).
routes.tax_note: A visa does not by itself decide Isle of Man tax residence.
routes.name: Common Travel Area (British and Irish citizens)
routes.summary: British and Irish citizens can move to the Isle of Man and live here without immigration permission. Only these two nationalities benefit; other EU and other-passport holders do not.
routes.requirements: Per the Department for Enterprise guide, 'only British and Irish passport holders are normally free to move to the Isle of Man and take up residence without the need for Immigration permission'. Irish citizens (EU group) and British citizens (OTHER group) only. Employment still needs an Isle of Man work permit under the Control of Employment Act 2014 unless the person is an 'Isle of Man worker' or the job is exempt (per the March 2026 immigration notice, Irish citizens need a work permit unless exempt).

routes.name: Business Migrant: Start-up visa
routes.summary: For first-time founders with an innovative, viable and scalable business idea endorsed by the Department for Enterprise. No investment threshold; leave is 2 years 4 months and cannot lead to settlement, but holders may switch to Innovator.
routes.requirements: Appendix X Part 6: letter of endorsement from the Department for Enterprise (innovation, viability, scalability; applicant has not previously established a trading business in the UK or Isle of Man; majority of working time spent managing the business on the Island); aged 18 or over; English B2; maintenance of GBP 945 in a personal account for 90 consecutive days, separate from any business funds. Endorsement application fee GBP 1,000. Leave 2 years 4 months, no extension, no ILR. Holder may also take other work. No public funds. No healthcare surcharge. Decision about 6 weeks from outside the UK and Isle of Man.
routes.physical_presence: Live in the Isle of Man and manage the business day to day (majority of working time)

routes.name: Business Migrant: Innovator visa
routes.summary: For experienced business people who set up, join or take over a business on the Island with at least GBP 50,000 of investment funds, endorsed by the Department for Enterprise. Leave is 3 years at a time, with settlement possible after 3 years.
routes.requirements: Appendix X Part 7: letter of endorsement; GBP 50,000 investment funds for each Innovator applicant (funds cannot be shared; not needed when progressing from Start-up or for an already established business endorsed earlier); business plan with at least 1 full-time permanent employee within 12 months and 3 within 36 months; majority of working time spent managing the business on the Island; English B2; maintenance GBP 945 for 90 consecutive days; aged 18 or over. Settlement (ILR) needs 3 years' continuous residence with at least GBP 50,000 invested, the business trading and tax-compliant, and 3 full-time permanent jobs held 12 months; absences up to 180 days in any 12 months. Endorsement fee GBP 1,000 at each stage. No other employment allowed.
routes.physical_presence: Live in the Isle of Man; no more than 180 days absent in any 12 months for settlement

routes.limited_places: Needs an employer who passes the labour market test; the Department decides each case (no right to a permit)
routes.fees_note: Entry clearance fee not listed on gov.im ('see form for fees'); CoE for entry clearance: no charge; SET W (ILR): GBP 3,226; work permit GBP 60 (employer).
routes.family: Partner and children can apply as dependants (Part 8 / Appendix FM). Partners of permit holders get an automatic 1-year work permit.
routes.tax_note: A visa does not by itself decide Isle of Man tax residence.
routes.name: Worker Migrant visa (Appendix W) and work permit
routes.summary: A job offer from an Isle of Man employer in an eligible occupation, with a Confirmation of Employment from the Immigration Service. Salary must be at least GBP 25,447.50 a year or the occupation rate, and the employer must first test the local market.
routes.requirements: Appendix W: valid Confirmation of Employment (CoE) in an eligible occupation (Appendix Skilled Occupations or Shortage Occupation List); salary at least the higher of GBP 25,447.50 a year or the occupation rate (for new applicants from 31 October 2025; new Worker Migrant rules from 1 June 2026); English language; maintenance funds under Appendix C (employer may instead undertake to maintain, GBP 1,270 a month for 3 months); the vacancy must not be fillable by a settled worker (Sequential Labour Market Test, unless exempt). No self-employment. Under the Control of Employment Act 2014 a work permit is also needed unless the holder has an 'immigration employment document' (a visa of this kind) or the job is exempt. ILR after 5 years' continuous residence (absences up to 180 days in a year) with employer confirmation of salary and English plus Life in the UK knowledge.
routes.physical_presence: Live and work on the Island; no more than 180 days absent in a year for settlement

routes.status_note: Free movement ended on 31 December 2020. The scheme was for people resident before 1 January 2021; its application deadline (30 June 2021 per gov.im) has passed. Not a route for someone arriving today.
routes.name: EU Settlement Scheme (Appendix EU)
routes.summary: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens who lived on the Island before 2021 could apply for status. New arrivals from the EU need a visa like anyone else.
routes.requirements: Residence in the Isle of Man before 1 January 2021. Closed to new arrivals; the Island's scheme is aligned with the UK EUSS under Appendix EU. No charge.

Dual citizenship not verified from an official source.
